description: Three pitted iron links, worn smooth where a harness rubbed. The Nightmule that wore it is still out there.
lore: There is a carter at the east crossing who pays nine gold a set for these and is not melting them. He is rebuilding the rig. He has the breeching, most of a collar, a bridle with one cheekpiece, a pad — all of it picked up off the ground behind [[monsters/dark_donkey|the mule that still keeps its route]] — and he is short two trace chains and a hame strap. Ask what he means to do with a finished harness and he will tell you flatly: put it on. Not to stop the animal. It has never minded being touched, and it has never once stopped. He wants to load it, and walk at its head, and be the voice up front, since the voice it halts for is not coming. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] has offered to name him the stops on the old road. He says he will take that when the rig is done.
gm_notes: The carter is unnamed and ready to use: eleven-odd years of buying junk iron toward one afternoon. Two ways it can land — the mule accepts the harness and walks its route with a man at its head, which is either the kindest scene on the east road or the saddest; or it walks straight through him, because he is not the voice. Do not decide in advance. Wendell's offer is the second hook: the old man has the route in his head and no one has ever wanted it this badly.
